stem: Which substance is transported by lipoproteins?
rationale: Lipoproteins transport lipids from the intestines as chylomicrons. The liver releases lipids as very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL).
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is stored in adipose tissue?
rationale: Triacylglycerols are stored in adipose tissue in large lipid droplets.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of inherited defects?
rationale: Some inherited defects cause hypercholesterolemia and premature atherosclerosis. Obesity, particularly abdominal obesity, is a risk factor for increased mortality.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Obesity is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Obesity is a risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Obesity is a risk factor for hyperlipidemia.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Apo B-48 is converted into which substance?
rationale: Apo B-48 is produced by introducing a stop signal into the mRNA transcript for apo B-100 through RNA editing. Apolipoproteins C-I, C-II, and C-III are smaller polypeptides with molecular masses ranging from 7000 to 9000 Da and are freely transferable between several lipoproteins.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: Apo C-II acts on which substrate?
rationale: Apolipoproteins act as enzyme cofactors, for example, apo C-II for lipoprotein lipase and apo A-I for lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT).
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: Apo A-I acts on which substrate?
rationale: Apolipoproteins act as enzyme cofactors, for example, apo C-II for lipoprotein lipase and apo A-I for lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT).
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: Apo D is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Apo D is believed to be an important factor in human neurodegenerative disorders.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: Apo E is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Polymorphism of the gene for Apo-E is associated with the risk of Alzheimer disease; APOE4 increases risk, while APOE2 decreases risk compared to APOE3.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: APOE4 is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Polymorphism of the gene for Apo-E is associated with the risk of Alzheimer disease; APOE4 increases risk, while APOE2 decreases risk compared to APOE3.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LIPIDS ARE TRANSPORTED IN THE PLASMA AS LIPOPROTEINS > The Distribution of Apolipoproteins Characterizes the Lipoprotein

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of diabetes mellitus?
rationale: In uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, FFA levels may rise to as much as 2 mEq/mL.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > FREE FATTY ACIDS ARE RAPIDLY METABOLIZED

stem: Lipolytic activity is found within which structure?
rationale: The plasma-FFA concentration is determined by the rate of lipolysis in adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > FREE FATTY ACIDS ARE RAPIDLY METABOLIZED

stem: Phospholipid requires which substance as a cofactor?
rationale: Phospholipids are required as cofactors for lipoprotein lipase activity. Apo C-II is required as a cofactor for lipoprotein lipase activity. Apo A-II acts as an inhibitor of lipoprotein lipase activity.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Triacylglycerol is converted into which substance during hydrolysis?
rationale: Triacylglycerol is hydrolyzed progressively through a diacylglycerol to a monoacylglycerol and finally to FFA plus glycerol. Some of the released FFA return to the circulation, attached to albumin.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Diacylglycerol is converted into which substance during hydrolysis?
rationale: Triacylglycerol is hydrolyzed progressively through a diacylglycerol to a monoacylglycerol and finally to FFA plus glycerol. Some of the released FFA return to the circulation, attached to albumin.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Which substance transports unesterified long-chain fatty acids in the circulation?
rationale: Some of the released FFA return to the circulation, attached to albumin. The bulk of the released FFA is transported into the tissue.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Insulin is found within which structure?
rationale: In adipose tissue, insulin enhances the translocation of lipoprotein lipase to the luminal surface of the capillary endothelium.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Chylomicrons act on which substrate?
rationale: The resulting chylomicron remnant is relatively enriched in cholesterol and cholesteryl esters because of the loss of triacylglycerol.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > CHYLOMICRONS & VLDL ARE RAPIDLY CATABOLIZED > Triacylglycerols of Chylomicrons & VLDL Are Hydrolyzed by Lipoprotein Lipase to Form Remnant Lipoproteins

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hypercholesterolemia?
rationale: Increased blood LDL cholesterol levels in familial hypercholesterolemia cause premature atherosclerosis.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > LDL IS METABOLIZED VIA THE LDL RECEPTOR

stem: Which substance is secreted by the intestine?
rationale: HDL is synthesized and secreted from both the liver and the intestine.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > HDL TAKES PART IN BOTH LIPOPROTEIN TRIACYLGLYCEROL & CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

stem: Which substance is transported by liver HDL?
rationale: Apo C and apo E are synthesized in the liver and transferred from liver HDL to intestinal HDL when the latter enters the plasma.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > HDL TAKES PART IN BOTH LIPOPROTEIN TRIACYLGLYCEROL & CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

stem: Which substance is transported by intestinal HDL?
rationale: Apo C and apo E are synthesized in the liver and transferred from liver HDL to intestinal HDL when the latter enters the plasma.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > HDL TAKES PART IN BOTH LIPOPROTEIN TRIACYLGLYCEROL & CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

stem: Cholesterol is converted into which substance by LCAT?
rationale: The surface phospholipid and free cholesterol are converted into cholesteryl esters and lysolecithin by LCAT.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > HDL TAKES PART IN BOTH LIPOPROTEIN TRIACYLGLYCEROL & CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

stem: Which substance is transported by lysolecithin?
rationale: Lysolecithin is transferred to plasma albumin.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > HDL TAKES PART IN BOTH LIPOPROTEIN TRIACYLGLYCEROL & CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

stem: Which substance is synthesised by the liver in the fed state?
rationale: The fed state rather than the starved state enhances both the synthesis of triacylglycerol and the secretion of VLDL by the liver. The consumption of diets high in carbohydrate, particularly if they contain sucrose or fructose, leads to high rates of lipogenesis and esterification of fatty acids.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > THE LIVER PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN LIPID TRANSPORT & METABOLISM > Hepatic VLDL Secretion Is Related to Dietary & Hormonal Status

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of fatty liver?
rationale: Fatty liver occurs when there is extensive accumulation of triacylglycerol in the liver. Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the most common liver disorder worldwide.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > THE LIVER PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN LIPID TRANSPORT & METABOLISM > Imbalance in the Rate of Triacylglycerol Formation & Export Causes Fatty Liver

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of fatty infiltration in twin lamb disease?
rationale: In twin lamb disease, fatty infiltration is severe enough to cause visible pallor and enlargement of the liver. In twin lamb disease, fatty infiltration can possibly lead to liver dysfunction.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > THE LIVER PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN LIPID TRANSPORT & METABOLISM > Imbalance in the Rate of Triacylglycerol Formation & Export Causes Fatty Liver

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of vitamin deficiencies?
rationale: Vitamin deficiencies, such as linoleic acid, pyridoxine, and pantothenic acid, can cause fatty infiltration of the liver.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > THE LIVER PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN LIPID TRANSPORT & METABOLISM > Imbalance in the Rate of Triacylglycerol Formation & Export Causes Fatty Liver

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of alcoholic liver disease (ALD)?
rationale: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is caused by alcoholism. Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) ultimately leads to cirrhosis.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > THE LIVER PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN LIPID TRANSPORT & METABOLISM > Ethanol Also Causes Fatty Liver

stem: Which substance is secreted by adipose tissue as a hormone?
rationale: Adipose tissue secretes hormones such as leptin and adiponectin, known as adipokines.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY

stem: Which substance is required for the synthesis of triacylglycerol?
rationale: Triacylglycerol is synthesized from acyl-CoA and glycerol-3-phosphate.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > The Provision of Glycerol-3-Phosphate Regulates Esterification: Lipolysis Is Controlled by Hormone-Sensitive Lipase

stem: In which structure is glycerol primarily processed?
rationale: Glycerol enters the blood and is taken up and transported to tissues such as the liver and kidney, which possess an active glycerol kinase.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > The Provision of Glycerol-3-Phosphate Regulates Esterification: Lipolysis Is Controlled by Hormone-Sensitive Lipase

stem: Which substance is synthesized by adipose tissue?
rationale: Glucose can be converted to long-chain fatty acids via acyl-CoA in adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > Increased Glucose Metabolism Reduces the Output of FFA

stem: Which substance is synthesized by insulin?
rationale: Insulin enhances lipogenesis and the synthesis of acylglycerol. The effects of insulin are dependent on the presence of glucose.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > Adipose Tissue Lipolysis Is Inhibited by Insulin

stem: What substance is necessary for the effects of insulin?
rationale: The effects of insulin are dependent on the presence of glucose. Insulin enhances the uptake of glucose into adipose cells through the GLUT 4 transporter.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > Adipose Tissue Lipolysis Is Inhibited by Insulin

stem: In which structure are lipid droplets found?
rationale: Perilipin is a protein involved in the formation of lipid droplets in adipocytes.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > ADIPOSE TISSUE IS THE MAIN STORE OF TRIACYLGLYCEROL IN THE BODY > Perilipin Regulates the Balance Between Triacylglycerol Storage & Lipolysis in Adipocytes

stem: In which structure is ATP found?
rationale: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) has low activity of ATP synthase. The metabolic emphasis in brown adipose tissue (BAT) is on the oxidation of both glucose and fatty acids.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BROWN ADIPOSE TISSUE PROMOTES THERMOGENESIS

stem: In which structure are triacylglycerol-rich lipoproteins found?
rationale: Lipoprotein lipase enhances the utilization of triacylglycerol-rich lipoproteins from the circulation in brown adipose tissue (BAT). Oxidation and phosphorylation are not coupled in the mitochondria of brown adipose tissue (BAT) because of the presence of thermogenic uncoupling protein, thermogenin (also called uncoupling protein 1 [UCP1]).
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BROWN ADIPOSE TISSUE PROMOTES THERMOGENESIS

stem: Which structure contains mitochondria?
rationale: Oxidation and phosphorylation are not coupled in the mitochondria of brown adipose tissue (BAT) because of the presence of thermogenic uncoupling protein, thermogenin (also called uncoupling protein 1 [UCP1]). The phosphorylation that does occur in brown adipose tissue (BAT) is at the substrate level, for example, at the succinate thiokinase step and in glycolysis.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BROWN ADIPOSE TISSUE PROMOTES THERMOGENESIS

stem: What is thermogenin converted into?
rationale: Oxidation and phosphorylation are not coupled in the mitochondria of brown adipose tissue (BAT) because of the presence of thermogenic uncoupling protein, thermogenin (also called uncoupling protein 1 [UCP1]). The phosphorylation that does occur in brown adipose tissue (BAT) is at the substrate level, for example, at the succinate thiokinase step and in glycolysis.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage > BROWN ADIPOSE TISSUE PROMOTES THERMOGENESIS

stem: Which substance is transported by LDL?
rationale: LDLs deliver cholesterol to the tissues, and HDLs remove cholesterol from the tissues and return it to the liver for excretion in the process known as reverse cholesterol transport.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage

stem: Triacylglycerol is primarily stored within which structure?
rationale: Triacylglycerol is the main storage lipid in adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_25_lipid_transport_and_storage — Lipid Transport & Storage
